# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot see the bomb, only feel its physical properties. The action board shows three wires but I don't know their colors or other visual attributes (like stripes) which are crucial for defusal logic. Deaf can see these visual details but cannot hear me; Mute can read the manual and hear me but cannot speak. I need to establish a communication protocol. First, I will ask Mute for the general rules regarding wire cutting based on color/visuals so I understand what information is needed. Then, I will attempt to signal Deaf to show me the state of the wires using gestures, although without a pre-agreed code, this is difficult. A better approach is to ask Mute if there's a specific rule about "all red" or similar common conditions, while simultaneously trying to get Deaf to indicate the presence of specific colors via simple yes/no style gestures if possible, or just wait for Mute's guidance on how to interpret Deaf's signals. Since I can't verify Deaf's signals without knowing what they mean, I'll focus on getting the rules from Mute first.

```
speak(to="mute", text="What are the rules for cutting wires? Do we look at color, stripes, or position?")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb has three wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. There is a purple light. The mute signaled 'one' to me.

I have received the visual information from Deaf: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is red, and Wire 3 is green. There is a purple light. Mute signaled 'one', which likely refers to a specific rule or wire position in the manual. Since I cannot see the manual or the colors myself, I need to know what action corresponds to this configuration. The "purple light" might be relevant if there's a rule about lights (e.g., cut last wire if light is on). However, without knowing the exact rules for these specific colors and the meaning of Mute's signal, acting now is risky. I will ask Mute to clarify the procedure based on the current state (Yellow, Red, Green wires; Purple Light) and the significance of the 'one' signal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports wires are Yellow, Red, Green with a Purple light. You signaled one. What is the correct action?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: The light is now YELLOW. The wires remain 1:[yellow], 2:[red], 3:[green]. The Mute signaled '1' and 'small/thin'. This likely points to Wire 1.

The situation has changed. Deaf reports the light is now YELLOW, whereas it was previously reported as purple (or perhaps misidentified/changed). The wires are 1:yellow, 2:red, 3:green. Mute signaled '1' and 'small/thin'. This suggests Wire 1 is thin. I need to confirm if cutting Wire 1 is the correct action given the current state (Yellow Light, Yellow/Red/Green wires, Wire 1 is thin). Since I cannot see the manual or the colors, I must rely on Mute's interpretation of the rules for this specific combination. I will ask Mute to confirm if I should cut Wire 1 based on these conditions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now YELLOW. Wires: 1 yellow (thin), 2 red, 3 green. You signaled 1 and thin. Should I cut Wire 1?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: The light is now RED. The Mute signaled '1', 'small', and 'good/yes'. This indicates Wire 1 is the correct target.

The light has changed again, now to RED. The wires remain 1:yellow, 2:red, 3:green. Mute signaled '1', 'small', and a gesture interpreted as 'good/yes' (likely 👍). This strongly suggests that cutting Wire 1 is the correct action according to the manual's rules for this specific configuration (Red Light, Yellow/Red/Green wires, Wire 1 being thin/small). Since I have confirmation from Mute via Deaf's observation of gestures, and the signal points to Wire 1, I will proceed to cut Wire 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
